newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU chocolate plan would have limited impact - study.
newsitem.headline: EU chocolate plan would have limited impact - study.

text.p: A new academic study shows that a European Commissiom proposal to allow limited use of non-cocoa fat in chocolate would not hurt cocoa producers, European chocolate producers said on Thursday.
The study by the Free University of Amsterdam concluded that only 33,000 tonnes of cocoa beans, or 1.3 percent of world demand, would be substituted.

Cocoa producing countries and development aid groups have said the Commission's proposal in April to allow up to five percent non-cocoa fat in chocolate could result in cocoa demand falling by up to 200,000 tonnes.

"This study will clarify the confusion surrounding the impact of the draft Directive on the ACP (African, Caribbean and Pacific) countries...," Arnold Van Hecke, director of Caobisco, representing the EU chocolate industry, said in a statement.
The study concluded that it would take up to eight years before the full impact of substitution was felt.
